newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH MINISTER SAYS ENERGY DISPATCHING BODY FORMED.
newsitem.headline: CZECH MINISTER SAYS ENERGY DISPATCHING BODY FORMED.

text.p: Czech Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy said on Friday his ministry and the country's power firms have established a long-awaited "Energy Dispatching Centre" to manage the national power grid.

Speaking at a news conference, Dlouhy said power producer CEZ a.s. , would have 20 percent voting rights in the body, as would the minstry and independent producers while the eight regional power distributors would have 40 percent of the vote.
"I consider this to be a very important moment for our energy sector," Dlouhy told reporters.
The dispatching centre will have the authority to regulate the national power grid, ensure supply from different sources and decide on needs for new power plants.
Dlouhy said the body's quorum for decision making would be 75 percent, and the threshold for making a strategic vote valid would be 85 percent.
Establishment of the dispatching centre had been delayed for months because of a failure to agree on the distribution of voting rights.

Last year CEZ, which generates about 75 percent of the country's electricity and runs the high-voltage national network, and some smaller companies set up a dispatching centre but regional distributors did not join and the ministry ruled the body unlawful.
